prompt: A clean, sharp, straight-on studio photograph, taken at a lost-property desk, of the FRONT face of a 2x2 pocket twist cube after a sequence of turns has been applied. The cube begins SOLVED in the standard Western colour scheme: UP is WHITE, DOWN is YELLOW, FRONT is GREEN, BACK is BLUE, RIGHT is RED, LEFT is ORANGE. From that solved state, apply EXACTLY this sequence of face turns in order, in standard cube notation: U R F R' U' F U R'. (A letter is a 90-degree clockwise turn of that face viewed from outside; a prime ' means counter-clockwise; a 2 means a half turn.) After the whole sequence, render ONLY the resulting FRONT face as a flat 2x2 grid of four coloured square stickers filling the frame, thin black lines between the four stickers, each sticker one flat solid colour from the six cube colours. No other faces, no cube body, no desk, no background, no text, no arrows, no labels.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show lost-property-desk studio photo of a 2x2 pocket twist cube's front face after an 8-turn sequence? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.
